text: Brad Pierce
Abstract

runs.text: Abstract

text: AI agents are making candidate code cheap. The harder problem is reaching independently accepted change. This paper asks what language an agent should act in and proposes a way to compare the alternatives. Hold the task, model, tools, acceptance contract, whole-loop budget, and risk policy fixed; vary the agent-facing representation and the execution contract that gives it meaning; then measure the cost and risk of accepted change. The design hypothesis is useful freedom: enough semantic territory to solve the real problem, but no more hazardous territory than the work requires. Hardware supplies the first sharp test. Across four RTL representation families, the representation that wins at first-pass correctness may not produce the most independently accepted changes under matched budgets and risk constraints. Trustworthy Change Yield records that possible ranking reversal as a preregistered scorecard and Pareto surface. The contribution is not a new universal language or metric, but a controlled comparison whose prediction can fail. This is a position paper and experimental agenda, not an empirical result.
